analyst_view.overall: Early view: a Funchal derby between two sides near the bottom, with Marítimo 15th on 8 points (a game in hand, the postponed trip to Estoril) and Nacional 13th on 10. Nacional are on their third coach of the season, João Henriques, and have just won 1-0 against Académico Viseu with a physical display, while Mitchell van der Gaag has moved Marítimo to a back three to stop the leaks (21 conceded in 10). Madeira weather has already postponed two games this month, so keep an eye on the forecast.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Nacional's last three league games all finished 1-0 (beating Braga and Académico Viseu at home, losing at Arouca in Henriques's debut), and van der Gaag's switch to three centre-backs is meant to close games down. Marítimo have scored only 9 in 10, so a nervy, low-scoring derby looks more likely than a shoot-out.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, split almost evenly. Marítimo's wing-backs will push crosses in, but Nacional under Henriques look content to defend deep and break, which tends to cap their own corner count. Nothing points clearly away from the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean higher: it is a local derby, both clubs are looking over their shoulder at the relegation places, and Nacional's recent wins were built on 'muscle', in Record's words. Derbies between struggling sides rarely stay calm for 90 minutes.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. I lean lower: Marítimo's attack has produced 9 goals in 10 games, and Nacional, once ahead, have been happy to sit on a lead. A back three against a deep block usually means long spells of slow possession rather than a flood of attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, which is high for two of the league's weaker attacks. Nacional have scored 11 in 11 and Marítimo 9 in 10, and with Bassouamina away with Congo during the break his sharpness is an unknown. I expect fewer clear efforts than the model suggests.
